headline: One child. Two timetables.
intro: Training that puts school and social care in the same room to sort out the clash points.

problem.scene: 10am Tuesday: Ellie's maths mock. And her review.
problem.question: Her maths teacher finds out when she doesn't turn up.
without: Moves in the middle of term
A personal education plan filled in, not used
with: School places arranged with the home
A written deal on who does what
problem.standards: The statutory guidance on promoting the education of looked-after and previously looked-after children expects a school place alongside a new home, and a PEP reviewed each term with the child.
problem.evidence: It works best with school and social care together, because hearing the other side is the point.

groups: Designated teachers, SENCOs and designated safeguarding leads
Social workers, personal advisers and independent reviewing officers
Foster, kinship and residential carers who attend PEP meetings
notes: No knowledge of the other system needed

outcomes: Describe a week for a child with a social worker, showing where the two timetables collide.
Identify the clash points in your area and who can fix each one.
Use Bronfenbrenner to explain why the link matters, and set out the designated teacher, virtual school head and social worker roles.
Apply the rules on education stability, including approval for moves in years 10 and 11.
Write personal education plan (PEP) targets with the child's views, linked to Pupil Premium Plus.
Agree in writing what school and social care will each do to protect a child's education.

The child's view changes what happens, and they are told how.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on the link between school and social care, including Darlington, where designated teachers designed their own programme with him, and a co-design workshop with around 200 Virtual School Heads at the NAVSH annual conference.
He led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education, and teachers are one of the largest groups he trains.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
